MATTHEVV.|57}}</noinclude>Hierusalem, and the Sonne of man shal be deliuered to the cheefe priestes and to the Scribes, and they shal condemne him to death, {{verse|chapter=20|verse=19}}† and shal deliuer him to the Gentiles to be mocked, & scourged, & crucified, and the third day he shal rise againe.⊣

{{verse|chapter=20|verse=20}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 10, 35.''}}* {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpon S. Iames day. ''Iul. 25.'' And ''S. Iohns ante portam Latinam Maij 6.''}}Then came to him the mother of the sonnes of Zebedee vvith her sonnes, adoring and desiring some thing of him. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=21}}† Who said to her, What wilt thou? She saith to him, Say that these my tvvo sonnes may sitte, one at thy right hand, and one at thy left hand in thy kingdom. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=22}}† And IESVS ansvvering, said, You knovv not vvhat you desire. Can you drinke of the cuppe that I shal drinke of? They say to him, We can. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=23}}† He saith to them, My cuppe in deede you shal drinke of: but to sitte at my right hand and left, is not mine to giue to you: but ‖ to vvhom it is prepared of my father.⊣ {{verse|chapter=20|verse=24}}† And the ten hearing it, vvere displeased at the tvvo brethren. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=25}}† And IESVS called them vnto him, and said, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 10, 41. Lu. 22, 25.''}}* You knovv that the princes of the gentiles {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Superiority is not here forbidden among Christians, neither Ecclesiastical nor temporal: but heathenish tyranny is forbidden, and humility commended.}}∷ ouerrule them: and they that are the greater, exercise povver against them. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=26}}† It shal not be so among you. but vvhosoeuer vvil be the greater among you, let him be your minister: {{verse|chapter=20|verse=27}}† and he that vvil be first among you, shal be your seruant. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=28}}† Euen as the ‖ Sonne of man is not come to be ministred vnto, but to minister, and to giue his life a redemption for many.⊣

{{verse|chapter=20|verse=29}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 10, 46.''}}* vvhen they vvent out from Iericho, a great multitude folovved him. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=30}}† And behold tvvo blinde men sitting by the vvay side, heard that IESVS passed by, and they cried out saying, Lord, haue mercie vpon vs, sonne of Dauid. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=31}}† And the multitude rebuked them that they should hold their peace. But they cried out the more, saying, Lord, haue mercie vpon vs, sonne of Dauid. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=32}}† And IESVS stoode, and called them, and said, VVhat vvil ye that I doe to you? {{verse|chapter=20|verse=33}}† They say to him, Lord, that our eies may be opened. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=34}}† And IESVS hauing compassion on them, touched their eies. And immediatly they savv, and folovved him.

{{c|{{sc|Chap. XX.}}}}

''1. In the morning.''] God called some in the morning, that is, in the beginning of the world, as Abel, Enoch, Noë, and other the iust and faithful of the first age: at the third houre, Abraham, Isaac, and Iacob, and the rest of their age: at the 6 houre of the day, Moyses, Aaron, and the rest: at the 9 houre, the Prophetes: at the eleuenth, that is, at the later end of the world, the Christian<noinclude>{{rh||H|Nations.}}</noinclude>
